title: Select a usable requirement basis before detailed design exists
goal: Establish sufficient requirements for dependent design without a mandatory intermediate approval.
context: Requirement analysis supplies proposed changes or justified reuse, while Functions and ARs may be unfinished.
trigger: The author has reconciled an incoming request with existing requirements.
preconditions: The requested scope and relevant project authority are identifiable.

interaction.action: Identifies the exact requirement and supporting analysis subjects, justified disposition, acceptance intent and unresolved questions.
Selects the usable basis within current authority and records the rationale without claiming independent approval.
Preserves the basis and permits authorized design without requiring an intermediate review record.

expected_outcome: The selected requirement basis supports design; final independent whole-change review and Verify remain required.

alternatives.condition: Existing requirements fully cover the request.
alternatives.outcome: The author reuses the existing requirements without artificial edits or mandatory reuse approval.

alternatives.condition: Required logical behavior and architectural allocations are not yet designed.
alternatives.outcome: A sufficient requirement basis may be accepted while the later design obligations remain explicit.

alternatives.condition: An optional formal review is explicitly relied on.
alternatives.outcome: Its exact support and limitations remain attributable and adverse or stale support is not silently ignored.

failures.condition: Material requirements remain ambiguous or authority is missing.
failures.outcome: Dependent work remains unresolved and exposes the necessary decision; absence of an approval record alone is not the blocker.

failures.condition: Material requirement subjects change after the assessment.
failures.outcome: Earlier approval retains its original meaning and is not silently applied to the revised basis.

sources.basis: User-selected requirement-first workflow and one mandatory whole-change Code Review gate. Proposed requirement analysis only; existing product contracts remain active until coordinated adoption. No new Function, AR, implementation or approval is inferred.

Document-based author assessment under the explicit Constitution exception confirms this Scenario as requirement-analysis knowledge. It is not independent review, executed product evidence or workflow activation.
Remove intermediate approvals; keep final independent whole-change review and verification. Preserve authoring responsibilities, evidence, applicable authority and original historical judgments.
